solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Salutary warning (12, two words)

blocks.note: surface reading: a cautionary message that does someone good
setter's reading: a practical example from which a lesson can be learnt, the whole clue serving as the definition

explanation.walkthrough: There is no separate wordplay here: the two words are simply a description of the phrase, a rarity in an Azed puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a striking practical example that teaches a lesson, typically a cautionary one.

clue.text: Old sword as goad, end of weapon going in

indicators.note: one item going in means it is placed inside the other word
'end of' keeps only the last letter of 'weapon'

blocks.note: a brod is a goad or prod, a Scots and dialect word
the final letter of weapon

explanation.surface: An antique sword used as a prod, its point going in.
explanation.definitionFit: Brond is an obsolete word for a sword, a variant of brand in its old sense of blade.

clue.text: Grain hostilities? Combine mostly limits that

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the word loses its final letter
to limit something is to hem it in, so the shortened word wraps around the one before

blocks.note: to combine is to join
hostilities amount to war

explanation.surface: A question about whether there is conflict over grain, with a combine harvester enclosing the field.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark and 'Combine' suggest farm machinery, but Combine is a plain verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: Jowari is the Indian name for durra, a kind of sorghum grown as a cereal crop.

clue.text: Lorry of a kind? Short answer: one that's gained access

blocks.note: curt means short or brusque
A is the standard abbreviation for answer
someone who has got in on the inside

explanation.surface: A terse reply about a lorry and someone who has broken into it.
explanation.definitionFit: A curtainsider is a lorry whose sides are canvas curtains that slide open for loading; the question mark admits it is one kind among many.

clue.text: Fans of sport, lives belonging to it when brought up

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing something up turns it so it reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: lives means exists, which is to say is
of expresses belonging, as in friend of mine
taken as written

explanation.surface: Sports fans whose lives belong to the game they were raised on.
explanation.definitionFit: Tifosi is the Italian word for passionate supporters, especially of football teams or Ferrari.

clue.text: Court unusually dividing river vessel, being responsible for performance

indicators.note: done unusually means not in the ordinary way, so the letters are rearranged
something dividing a pair splits them by sitting between, so it goes inside

blocks.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
the letters of court rearranged
a ship is a vessel

explanation.surface: A legal case splitting a river boat's owners over who must deliver.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters sit between the river and the vessel, which are read as a single phrase in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Executorship is the role of an executor, who is responsible for carrying out, or performing, the terms of a will.

clue.text: Group capturing hearts, once close

indicators.note: capturing something means holding it inside, so one word encloses the other

blocks.note: a set is a group
H is the abbreviation for hearts in card games

explanation.surface: A band winning over hearts, as in close-knit days gone by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' marks the definition as archaic: shet is an old form of shut.
explanation.definitionFit: To shet is an obsolete word for shut, which is to close.

clue.text: Pacific islander with nothing sheltered in rain tree

indicators.note: something sheltered in another is kept within it, so it goes inside

blocks.note: the saman is the rain tree, a tropical American tree
O is the zero shape for nothing

explanation.surface: An islander with no possessions sheltering from rain under a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rain tree' reads as weather and tree, but it is one name: the saman.
explanation.definitionFit: A Samoan is a native of Samoa, an island group in the South Pacific.

clue.text: Recover from being pale, entering form of therapy

indicators.note: a word entering another goes inside it

blocks.note: OT is occupational therapy
a pale is a boundary or limit, as is a verge

explanation.surface: Getting over looking pallid after starting a course of treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pale' looks like an adjective about health; here it is the noun meaning boundary, as in beyond the pale.
explanation.definitionFit: Overget is an archaic word meaning to get over, that is to recover from something.

clue.text: Sketch Queen among unruly corgis? Not good

indicators.note: not here tells us to leave out the letter for the word that follows
unruly dogs will not stay in order, so the letters are rearranged
one thing among others is placed in their midst

blocks.note: taken as written, before shortening and rearranging
G is the abbreviation for good
QU is a dictionary abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: A picture of the Queen amid her badly behaved corgis, implying they are naughty.
explanation.walkthrough: The Queen's corgis were famous; the two-letter QU, rather than the usual R or ER, is what makes this work.
explanation.definitionFit: A croquis is a rough preliminary drawing, a French borrowing for a sketch.

clue.text: Irritation for old poet — he's taken in by clown using dialect words

indicators.note: being taken in by something means being held inside it

blocks.note: a chuff is a dialect word for a boor or clown
a is a dialect form of he
gives no letters: it flags that the pronoun and the clown are both dialect forms

explanation.surface: An old poet annoyed that a clown speaking in dialect has fooled him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'using dialect words' tells the solver that both the pronoun and the clown are given in their dialect forms.
explanation.definitionFit: Chauff is Spenser's form of chafe, so it means irritation in the work of an old poet.

clue.text: Being so makes car drive off, instinctively (4, two words)

blocks.clueFragment: Being so makes car drive off
blocks.note: if car is put inside the outer pair of letters this wordplay calls for, the result is a verb meaning to drive off

explanation.surface: Instinctive panic that makes a car speed away.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: put CAR IN S..E and you get SCARE, which means drive off. The answer is the Latin for in itself.
explanation.definitionFit: In se, Latin for in itself, describes something intrinsic, which is near enough to instinctive or by nature.

clue.text: What Scot's to do, making his hollow with end of pick?

definitions.text: What Scot's to do, making his hollow with end of pick?

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of the following word to add on

blocks.note: how is the Scots word for a hollow, the Scot's own
the final letter of pick

explanation.surface: A Scot scooping out a hole with the point of a pickaxe.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition and also the wordplay: a Scot's hollow plus the last letter of pick.
explanation.definitionFit: Howk is Scots for dig or scoop out, which is what someone does making a hollow with a pick.

clue.text: They've special privileges, returning lake in boggy ground

indicators.note: something returning goes back the way it came, so the word reads backwards
in places one word inside the other

blocks.note: a fen is marshy, boggy land
meer is an old spelling of mere, a lake

explanation.surface: Privileged people coming back to a lake set in marshland.
explanation.walkthrough: The usual spelling of lake would not fit; the variant with a double E is in Chambers.
explanation.definitionFit: Freemen hold the freedom of a city or borough, which carries special rights and privileges.

clue.text: ~Amber tincture~ getting a solicitor half cut?

indicators.note: cutting a word by half leaves only its first half

blocks.note: an is the form of the indefinite article a before a vowel
an attorney is the American term for a solicitor or lawyer

explanation.surface: A drunk lawyer reaching for a brownish drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half cut' is British slang for tipsy, which colours the surface; cryptically it halves the lawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatto (annatto) is an orange-yellow dye from a tropical tree, used to colour cheese and butter.

clue.text: Men in cast possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests one of several arrangements, so the letters are rearranged
in places one word inside the other

blocks.note: the letters of cast rearranged
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Perhaps the men who make up the cast of a play.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition and the wordplay at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors are the performers who make up the cast of a play or film, so men in a cast may be actors.

clue.text: Grass as fodder like veg (nip off) in leaf

indicators.note: the bracket says to nip off the matching letters, which is removing them from the end of the vegetable
in places the earlier words inside the last one

blocks.note: a leaf of a book is a page
like and as both express similarity
a turnip is a vegetable

explanation.surface: Grass fed to livestock, compared to vegetables with the tips cut, inside a leaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nip' is both the instruction verb and the letters removed: the vegetable ends in exactly those three.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasturage is grazing land or the grass growing on it, eaten by animals as fodder.

clue.text: Who'll render France lawful when it strays?

definitions.text: Who'll render France lawful when it strays?

indicators.note: a word that strays wanders off, so those letters leave the word for lawful

blocks.note: F is the international vehicle code for France
licit means lawful
these are the letters that stray away

explanation.surface: Who will make France law-abiding when people go astray?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: a French cop restores order when someone strays.
explanation.definitionFit: Flic is French slang for a police officer, whose job is to keep France within the law.

clue.text: Disguised, travel round Austria in a mask

indicators.note: something disguised has its appearance altered, so the letters are rearranged
going round something means surrounding it

blocks.note: the letters of travel rearranged
A is the international vehicle code for Austria

explanation.surface: Touring Austria in disguise, wearing a mask.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disguised' looks like the definition and 'in a mask' like padding; it is the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: Larvate means masked or concealed, from Latin larva, a ghost or mask.

clue.text: In Mideast one duly made to suffer barbaric punishment

indicators.note: in says the answer is found inside the run of words that follows

blocks.note: inside the letters of these words

explanation.surface: Someone in the Middle East duly sentenced to a brutal punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: To be stoned is to be pelted with stones, a cruel form of execution or punishment.

clue.text: Spectator's left entranced by grand exterior

indicators.note: entranced is read as taken inside, so the answer lies within the following words

blocks.note: inside the letters of these words

explanation.surface: An onlooker left spellbound by an imposing facade.
explanation.walkthrough: In heraldry the right of a shield is named from its bearer's view, so to someone looking at it that side is on their left.
explanation.definitionFit: Dexter is the heraldic term for the shield's right-hand side, which appears on the viewer's left.

clue.text: If with mean scraps…you may have got this

definitions.text: If with mean scraps…you may have got this

indicators.note: scraps read as a verb means breaks up, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: If all you eat is meagre scraps, you may be suffering this.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition and the wordplay; 'scraps' looks like a noun for leftovers but works as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A famine is extreme scarcity of food, which is what living on mean scraps implies.

clue.text: Circulation of survey, say, Liberal one in general

indicators.note: in places the earlier letters inside the following word

blocks.note: main means general, as in the main body
L is the abbreviation for Liberal
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A Liberal general sending out a questionnaire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'general' looks like an army officer but is an adjective meaning main.
explanation.definitionFit: A mail-in is a survey or ballot distributed and returned by post, so circulating a survey is an example.

clue.text: Resorts which anyone can go to in southern county

indicators.note: in places the film rating inside the county

blocks.note: Hants is the standard abbreviation for Hampshire, a county on England's south coast
U is the British film certificate meaning suitable for anyone

explanation.surface: Holiday spots open to all in a county in the south of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'which anyone can go to' sounds like a description of the resorts, but it is the universal film rating.
explanation.definitionFit: Haunts are places someone frequents, just as resorts can mean places people habitually go.

clue.text: Small portion in Scotland? South denied something similar

indicators.note: a letter that is denied is refused entry, so it is taken out of the word

blocks.note: a taste is a small portion too, something similar to the defined word
S is the abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: A wee Scottish portion, the south refused anything like it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'something similar' refers back to the definition: a word for a small portion, which loses its S.
explanation.definitionFit: Tate is Scots for a small portion or tuft, such as a pinch or lock of something.

clue.text: Worried about genetic identifier attached to another organ

indicators.note: about means around, so one word surrounds the other

blocks.note: ate means worried or gnawed at, as in what's eating you
DNA profiling identifies people genetically

explanation.surface: Anxious about a DNA test linking someone to a donated organ.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology adnate describes a part grown fused to another, such as an anther joined to its filament.

clue.text: At least four cups once cursed that'll need polishing

blocks.note: each bra has two cups, so more than one bra means at least four
sware is an archaic past tense of swear

explanation.surface: Several trophy cups, sworn at in the past, that someone must buff up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cups' suggests trophies; the plural of the item with two cups is what gives at least four.
explanation.definitionFit: Brassware is objects made of brass, which tarnish and need regular polishing.

clue.text: Spiritual father, last to take lead in a hostelry

indicators.note: the final letter is told to go to the front, moving the end to the start

blocks.note: taken as written
a pub is a hostelry

explanation.surface: A priest who is always last to the pub and then leads the way.
explanation.definitionFit: Bapu, meaning father in Gujarati and Hindi, is a title of respect given especially to Gandhi as a spiritual leader.

clue.text: Snack between meals, always with a slice of bacon on

indicators.note: a single slice of the word is just its first letter

blocks.note: the opening letter of bacon
ever means always

explanation.surface: A between-meals nibble that always comes topped with a bit of bacon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' in a down clue puts the bacon letter on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Bever is a dialect word for a light snack or drink taken between main meals.

clue.text: Opera star making comeback by way of protein

indicators.note: a comeback runs back the other way, so the word reads backwards

blocks.note: a diva is a leading female opera singer
in can mean by way of, as in the form of

explanation.surface: A soprano returning to the stage on a high-protein diet.
explanation.definitionFit: Avidin is a protein found in egg white that binds biotin.

clue.text: Reynard's tail behind, brushlike?

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: the final letter of Reynard
aft means behind, towards the back of a ship

explanation.surface: A fox's tail trailing behind like a brush.
explanation.walkthrough: A fox's tail is called its brush, so 'brushlike' seems literal; it refers to the British idiom daft as a brush.
explanation.definitionFit: The British saying 'daft as a brush' means very silly, so something brushlike is, jokingly, foolish.

clue.text: American anger once over online depository for world news

indicators.note: turned over means read the other way round

blocks.note: US is the abbreviation for American
tene is an archaic word for grief or anger

explanation.surface: American fury in the past over a global online news site.
explanation.definitionFit: Usenet is the early worldwide network of discussion groups where posts and news were stored and shared.

clue.text: Suffering that boy's held in, a paragon of good behaviour

indicators.note: being held in means being kept inside the other word

blocks.note: pain is suffering
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A boy confined while suffering, held up as a model of good conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: A paladin was one of Charlemagne's knights, hence any chivalrous champion or model of virtue.

clue.text: Following greeting Top of the Pops?

blocks.note: f is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
ave is Latin for hail, a greeting

explanation.surface: After a hello, the name of a famous TV chart show.
explanation.walkthrough: Top of the Pops was a long-running BBC chart show, and 'Top of' looks like an instruction to take the first letter of Pops; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A fave is a favourite, the one at the top of someone's choices, or pops.

clue.text: Let out in prison, one walks tall

indicators.note: out here means wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged
in places the rearranged letters inside the prison word

blocks.note: stir is slang for prison
the letters of let rearranged

explanation.surface: Released from jail, someone strides proudly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let out' reads as released; split, it is the fodder and its indicator. Walks tall sounds figurative but is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A stilter is someone who walks on stilts, and so literally walks tall.

clue.text: Crepes hornet spoilt — it's beneath the crust

indicators.note: something spoilt is damaged out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Pancakes ruined by a wasp, with something under the crust.
explanation.walkthrough: The kitchen picture makes the crust sound like pastry; it is the Earth's crust.
explanation.definitionFit: The centrosphere is the Earth's central core region, lying below the crust.
